The Fall
This game had terrible controls but was a great experience. It really should have been a point-and-click, but once you get past that the sci-fi atmosphere is really great, and the story is enjoyable.

The basic premise is that you're a sentient space suit whose owner has passed out, and you're trying to rescue him. One of my top picks last year.

 

Defense Grid 2
This one is a solid tower-defense experience, but I didn't like it quite as much as the first game. The mechanics were pretty similar, with a few new additions - and while the voice actor from the previous game is in this one, he's overshadowed by a cast of other characters. This makes it a lot less compelling in my opinion. The story is a continuation too, so if you haven't played the first one I'd recommend doing that before you play this. (it's not totally required, but this will be much more meaningful if you do)

 

Ironclad Tactics
This is a solid turn-based strategy experience with a cute story told in comic book style alongside it. Basically an alternate history where steam-powered robots are the form of combat. I wasn't in love with this game, it just didn't click with me, but it is very well done. So if you like this genre it's worth taking a look at.

 

Anomaly 2
This game (and the previous one) is a reverse-tower-defense game. That means you're playing the enemies driving between the towers, trying to make it to the end goal. I had issues with Anomaly Warzone Earth, but this sequel solved all those and is a much better experience.

There are two parts to the game and they work together really well - the first is picking your route by choosing which direction to go at intersections. Secondly you also play the commander, which runs alongside the trucks, healing them and doing things like stunning particularly powerful towers. I'd recommend giving this one a shot even if you don't like tower defense games.

 

Killing Floor
The sequel to this game is currently in early access (probably for the next 6 months), but for a couple bucks this is a great co-op experience. You fight off hordes of zombies with different special abilities, working to use your classes together. One person might be the sharpshooter, another might take out big enemies with shotguns, and a third person might light all the small ones on fire with a flamethrower.

It's important to level up, because you get perks as you get to higher levels - for example the firebug's smg starts lighting things on fire, and he gets complete immunity to flaming enemies. The only downside is that this leveling can take a long time for some classes - and that's one of the things they're improving in the sequel.

 

Saints Row 4
If you liked Saints Row 3 you'll probably enjoy this one - it's more of the same over-the-top action, but this time you also have superhero powers. Cars and planes are almost obsolete since you can run faster and fly on your own, and this makes getting around much more pleasant. Really it has every activity and character the previous game had, rebranded differently, but has a more comic book flavor.

Oh and the title intro to this game is absolutely fantastic.

 

Windosill
This game is super short - under an hour, but I always recommend it when it's on a deep sale - and also as a gift instead of something stupid like Bad Rats. The levels are really well designed, and a lot of fun to play around with - it's probably more of a toy/experience than a game.

The whole goal is to eventually get the level to give you a cube that opens the door to the next one - but they're so weirdly designed that it usually isn't obvious until you've played with all the elements of the level. Very cool.

 

Continue?9876543210
It takes a little while to figure out the "rules" of this weird cyber world and how to properly survive more than a couple levels. To me it felt a bit too random and jumbled to be enjoyable, but it's not a bad game.

The reason it is so chaotic is that you're playing a computer game character that's died, and is now fighting to avoid being erased completely. That's why the worlds are so chaotic and arbitrary - they're other fragments of places that haven't been erased yet. You'll run into a lot of NPCs asking questions, and have to figure out solutions to get bonuses - all while having a very limited amount of time before each level collapses.

 

BIT.TRIP Beat/Void
Much like BIT.TRIP Runner, these games are music based - you perform actions along with the music. Void is about growing by catching certain bits, while shrinking to avoid others. Beat is a pong like experience where you reflect different patterns of bits being thrown at you (at increasing speeds). I wasn't particularly enamored with Void, but Beat is probably my second favorite of this series, after Runner.

 

Hammerwatch
I gave this dungeon crawler a try a while ago, and just didn't find it very compelling (on top of the controls being a bit rough - you can only aim straight). This made it a bit slower than it should have been, but still wasn't particularly challenging. Cute pixel graphics, mediocre gameplay.
